title: Instagram Renamed Its AI Label So People Would Actually Get It
hook: 'AI creator' sounded like a job title. 'AI-generated profile' says what it means — the person in the photos does not exist.
key_points: Instagram is acting against fake AI-influencer accounts that pose as real people, per The Verge.
The 'AI creator' label is being renamed 'AI-generated profile' to remove the ambiguity.
'AI creator' read as a human who makes AI content; the new wording says the persona itself is synthetic.
Meta said people don't like discovering a profile is fake after the fact.
The label is account-level — it flags the persona, not each individual post.
Labels only catch accounts that get labeled; undisclosed fakes still rely on your own judgment.
content_html: Instagram is moving against fake AI-influencer accounts — profiles built around a person who doesn't exist, which have gotten steadily harder to spot. Alongside enforcement, it's changing what the disclosure actually says: the "AI creator" label becomes "AI-generated profile."
extra_html:
That rename does more work than it looks like. On social platforms "creator" is a job description, so "AI creator" parsed naturally as a human being who makes AI stuff — which is a completely different thing from the human in these photos is not real. Meta's own explanation, per The Verge, is that people don't like finding out after the fact that a profile they'd been following was synthetic.

The useful lesson generalizes past Instagram. Labels are only as good as the words on them, and only work on content that gets labeled. This one is account-level: it tags the persona, not each post, and it does nothing about a fake account that slipped through undisclosed. Platform disclosure is a floor, not a substitute for noticing when an account's photos are a little too flawless and its comments a little too generic.

related.title: AI 'Creators' Are Getting Harder to Spot
related.hook: AI influencers used to be easy to clock — too-smooth skin, an uncanny stare. The tells are vanishing, and fully synthetic 'creators' now slip into feeds without announcing themselves.

related.title: Spotify Will Badge AI Artists — and Stop Recommending Them
related.hook: From mid-September, artists that 'do not represent a real person' get an AI Persona badge, and Spotify keeps them out of your recommendations. Labeling plus demotion, not a ban.

related.title: Spotting AI-Made Content
related.hook: There are real tells for AI text and images — but they're fading fast, and 'AI detector' tools are unreliable. The durable skill is judging the source, not squinting at the pixels.

flashcards.prompt: Why was 'AI creator' a confusing label for a synthetic influencer account?

choices.text: It read like a human who makes AI content, rather than a persona that isn't a person
It implied the account was owned by an AI company
It suggested every post had been fact-checked

flashcards.explanation_html: "Creator" is a job title on social platforms, so the old label sounded like a profession. "AI-generated profile" states plainly that the persona is synthetic.

flashcards.prompt: What does an account-level AI label tell you — and what doesn't it?
flashcards.back_html: It says the persona is synthetic. It doesn't vet individual posts, and it can't flag the fake accounts that were never labeled in the first place.
